notes: Baba Farid University of Health Sciences (BFUHS), Faridkot counsels Punjab's 50% state quota in government colleges and all seats in private colleges, private universities and minority institutions, in three rounds and a stray vacancy round. None of the documents cited on this page is on the official site any more: BFUHS has taken its 2025-26 files off its website, so we read BFUHS's own files from copies kept by the Internet Archive, and name each document without a link.

r1.title: Round 1
who: Candidates registered with BFUHS by the last date, with the application fee paid. Your eligibility and medical fitness are checked at the allotted college when you report.

In 2025-26 applications closed on 03.11.2025; the provisional result came out on 27.11.2025 (some entries corrected on 28.11.2025), and joining, revised in line with MCC's schedule, was set for 02.12.2025 to 07.12.2025.
opts: Pay the six-month fee online (government colleges Rs 50,000 for basic sciences or Rs 62,500 for clinical subjects; private colleges Rs 1,37,500 or Rs 3,42,500, private-college diplomas (DA, DCH) Rs 2,05,000; NRI-quota seats pay a first instalment in US dollars instead), then report to the allotted college with your originals within the time given; the college checks your eligibility and medical fitness. If you don't pay, the allotment is cancelled; if you don't report in time, the seat is cancelled.
In case candidate failed to deposit the fee through online portal, the provisional allotment will be treated as cancelled.
The seat is cancelled and goes back into the pool. No penalty is stated, and a registered candidate stays eligible for Round 2.

Candidate’s who will not opt/forgo the seats in first counseling or have not attended the 1st counseling but are registered with the BFUHS, shall still be eligible for 2nd round of counseling of State of Punjab.

Round 1 is the only round with a free exit. Apply in writing to the college by the date BFUHS sets; in 2025-26 that was 5 PM on 18.12.2025, after two extensions. If you then take part in no later round, the fees you paid for the seat are refunded without penalty once all rounds are over; the application fee is never refunded. You can still come back: Round 2 let free-exit candidates log in again, and Round 3 asked them for a security deposit 'equivalent to penalty'.

Candidate’s who will surrender the seat in writing after joining in 1st round of online counseling within stipulated period and who will not participate in any subsequent rounds, their all fee will be refunded without any penalty.
Surrendering a Round 1 seat you didn't upgrade in Round 2, after the free exit has closed, is one of the cases in which the prospectus forfeits the refundable security deposit.
Candidate allotted a seat in round 1 & not upgraded in round 2, but surrenders the seat after stipulated time given for free exit.
gaps: the final Round 1 choice-filling dates: BFUHS's revised Round 1 schedule is listed in the Internet Archive but couldn't be retrieved.
any rule for candidates holding an all-India, deemed or central seat in Round 1 or Round 2.

r2.title: Round 2
who: Registered candidates with no Round 1 seat (Round 1 allottees who didn't join included), Round 1 joiners who want an upgrade, free-exit candidates, candidates whose Round 1 seat was cancelled over a category or disability claim, and new registrants, who pay the application fee. All submit willingness with a refundable security deposit: Rs 25,000 for government colleges (Rs 10,000 SC/BC/PwD) or Rs 2,00,000 for private colleges. Fees already paid for a Round 1 seat count towards it, and anyone who has already paid more than Rs 2,00,000 pays no more.
If you're happy with your Round 1 seat, you needn't take part.
pr: p.21

In 2025-26 willingness and fresh registration were set for 10.12.2025 to 11.12.2025; after the schedule was revised, choices closed at 5 PM on 24.12.2025, the result was set for 26.12.2025 (revised result 27.12.2025) and joining for 28.12.2025 to 30.12.2025.
opts: The fee you paid for the Round 1 seat is adjusted; you pay only the difference, if any. If you are upgraded and then don't join the new seat, the deposit is forfeited like any Round 2 non-joiner's.
Fee adjusted; don't join: deposit lost
In case seat is upgraded/changed in the 2nd round of counselling, the tuition fee deposited at the time of first counselling will be adjusted and only difference in fee, if any, has to be deposited.

You lose the security deposit, and the prospectus adds that a penalty 'shall be imposed' under a 2018 gazette notification we don't hold. You can come back for Round 3 only with a fresh registration (paying the application fee again) and a new deposit.
No, it is not mandatory to join the allotted seat, however, in case the candidate does not join, the refundable security deposit will be forfeited.

You may resign a Round 2 seat within the period BFUHS sets, but leaving it, or a Round 1 seat you still hold, forfeits the deposit. In 2025-26 joined Round 1 and 2 seats could be surrendered with forfeiture until 4 PM on 07.01.2026, a date later moved to 30.01.2026 and then to 5 PM on 03.02.2026, with MCC's schedule. The first Round 3 schedule adds that anyone who resigned in its window (then ending 07.01.2026) can't take part in later rounds, though elsewhere it lets Round 2 forfeiture exits come back with a fresh registration (see Round 3); whether that carried over to the later dates isn't stated.

Once the applicants join the 2nd round seat, he/she will be allowed to leave/resign the seat within stipulated period of time. However, in case the candidate leaves/resign/surrender the seat allocated in round two or already allotted seat in round one, refundable security deposit will be forfeited.
gaps: any rupee penalty beyond the deposit: the prospectus defers to the Medical Council of India's gazette notification of 05.04.2018, which isn't among our documents.

whether a Round 1 joiner who is upgraded in Round 2 and doesn't join the new seat keeps the Round 1 seat: no Round 2 document says (the Round 3 schedule says an upgraded joiner's earlier seat is vacated automatically).

r3.title: Round 3
who: Registered candidates without a seat, Round 1 and 2 joiners who want an upgrade, Round 2 non-joiners with a fresh registration and deposit, and new registrants after the cut-off was lowered in January 2026; anyone registering afresh pays the application fee again. Anyone holding an all-India seat is excluded, using MCC's list, and the schedule set a revised result 'after weeding out All India Quota Joined candidates upto round 3'.

Round 1 and 2 joiners who want to try for an upgrade submit willingness with a security 'equivalent to the penalty amount' and needn't surrender their seat; the schedule says they can't surrender it once Round 3 choice filling starts, upgraded or not (but see Not stated). Joiners who don't submit willingness can't take part. A Round 2 depositor who got no seat needn't deposit again, but must still submit willingness.

The Government's 2025 corrigendum converts seats still vacant after reserved-category and NRI candidates run out into the management quota's general pool in Round 3, or as MCC's guidelines direct. The Round 2 schedule also lists institutional-preference seats for conversion; the Round 3 schedule names only NRI and reserved seats.

In 2025-26 registration, willingness with the security deposit and application edits all closed at 5 PM on 22.01.2026. Choices opened on 27.01.2026 and, after MCC put its Round 3 choice locking on hold, were extended to 5 PM on 03.02.2026. BFUHS's later Round 3 schedule had set the result for 06.02.2026 and joining for 10.02.2026 to 4 PM on 13.02.2026; the extension notice said the rest of the schedule would follow.
opts: Your earlier seat is vacated at once and offered to others in the same round; you have no claim on it. If you then don't join the new seat, you're left with no seat, the deposit is forfeited and you can't take part in any further round. The fee is adjusted, except any penalty: you pay any balance, or the excess is refunded.
Once, the seat gets upgraded in Round-3, the previous gets vacated automatically and offered to the candidate as per merit in the same round. Thus, no claim can be made on the previous seat.
The penalty is imposed, the deposit is forfeited, and you can't take part in any further round.

If the candidate does not join the allotted seat of Round 3 the penalty will be imposed and the security amount deposited will be forfeited as per rules and the candidate will be ineligible to participate in any further round.
You can't resign or leave a Round 3 seat, and you can't take part in the stray round or any later counselling.
Once, the candidate joined the seat will not be allowed to vacate/surrender/leave/resign from allotted 3rd round seat.
gaps: the rupee 'penalty amount': the Round 3 schedule has everyone submit willingness with the usual security (Rs 25,000, or Rs 10,000 SC/BC/PwD, for government colleges; Rs 2,00,000 for private), and the prospectus has joiners pay its balance after their fee is adjusted, but the schedule's FAQ calls joiners' security 'equivalent to the penalty amount', and no document gives a penalty in rupees.

whether a joined candidate who surrenders with forfeiture before Round 3 may still take part in it: the Round 3 schedule says a Round 2 forfeiture exit may, with a fresh registration and deposit, but a note on its last page says anyone who resigns in that window may not.

whether a Round 1 or 2 joiner could still surrender after Round 3 choice filling began on 27.01.2026: the Round 3 schedule says no, but BFUHS's later schedule and notice kept the surrender-with-forfeiture window open to 30.01.2026 and then 03.02.2026.
the final Round 3 result and joining dates: no BFUHS notice after the choice-filling extension of 30.01.2026 is among our documents.
what BFUHS's notice of 06.01.2026 changed: the Internet Archive lists it, but it couldn't be retrieved.

stray.title: Stray round
who: Anyone allotted a seat in Round 3 can't take part, and no seat can be upgraded or shifted after Round 3.
opts: Under the following circumstances the refundable security deposit will be forfeited: i. Where a Candidate has been allotted a seat in Round 2 or subsequent rounds (round3, stray vacany/further rounds) and does not report/joins at the allotted college to complete the admission process.
The prospectus says a seat joined in Round 3 or any further round can't be resigned, and bars you from any further counselling; it doesn't name the stray round separately.

Candidates who have joined the allotted seat in Round 3 and further rounds of counselling will not be allowed to resign and will also be ineligible to take part in further rounds of any type of counselling as per directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India dated 16.12.2021 passed in Special Leave to Appeal (C) No. 10487 of 2021 Nihila P.P Vs Medical Counselling Committee and ors.
gaps: the stray round's dates, whether candidates with no seat could take part, and whether the 'further rounds' rule on resigning was applied to it: BFUHS's stray-round notices aren't among the documents we hold.

after.title: Leaving the course
chips: In-service bond: up to Rs 50 lakh
opts: Candidates other than in-service PCMS doctors give a Rs 30 lakh indemnity bond or bank guarantee for 3 years' service after the course; all-India quota candidates, Rs 20 lakh for 2 years. These amounts come from the 2025 corrigendum; the 2023 notification text still printed beside it says Rs 15 lakh for 2 years and Rs 10 lakh for 1 year. Not serving leads to recovery of the bond money, and the bond is extended if you go on to higher study.

They give the bond 'as notified by the Health Department', and the prospectus prints that Department's memo of 25-06-2019, which sets: incentive-marks category Rs 50 lakh for 10 years (degree) or Rs 25 lakh for 6 years (diploma); others Rs 15 lakh for 5 years (degree) or Rs 10 lakh for 3 years (diploma). Not serving means the bond is invoked, counts as gross misconduct and can get your registration struck off; leaving the course midway debars you from applying again (in the incentive category, from that category). The notification also cites Health Department orders of 2020 that aren't printed; whether they changed these amounts isn't stated.

Their separate notification, printed in the same prospectus with no corrigendum, asks Rs 15 lakh for 2 years' service (all-India quota Rs 10 lakh for 1 year), and keeps the exception for no job offer within six months or a senior residency in a Punjab government college, subject to availability.

In the notification's fee schedule, printed after its private-college fees, a college may ask for a bond or bank guarantee that you'll pay the balance fee for the whole course even if you leave midway. And if you drop out and later seek a fresh PG admission, you pay the fee for the full course (3 years for a degree, 2 for a diploma), plus any bond.
gaps: whether the 2023 rule that the bond doesn't apply if Punjab makes no job offer within six months of your passing, or if you join a senior residency in a Punjab government college, subject to availability, still holds for the Rs 30 lakh bond: the corrigendum says the rest of the notification stays as it is but doesn't restate it.
whether the Rs 30 lakh bond covers private-college seats: the corrigendum doesn't say; the notification's bond paragraphs sit in its section on government colleges.

which bond an in-service PCMS doctor outside the incentive category gives: the memo says Rs 15 lakh for 5 years (Rs 10 lakh for 3 years, diploma), but the notification's heading for that category and the corrigendum's Rs 30 lakh row both read 'Candidates other than in service Regular PCMS/PCMS'. Doctors serving in other departments, boards or corporations also follow their employer's NOC terms.

reg: Application fee Rs 5,900 (Rs 2,950 for SC; the two January 2026 Round 3 notices say SC/BC), including GST, non-refundable, and paid again on a fresh registration in a later round. NRI-quota applicants pay US$ 1,500 for the eligibility certificate and US$ 1,500 as application fee, with form fees of Rs 2,500 and Rs 3,000; the two dollar fees aren't refunded, and the prospectus doesn't say whether these replace the Rs 5,900. At admission, a one-time library fee: Rs 9,000 (MD/MS) or Rs 6,000 (diploma).
dep: From Round 2 on: Rs 25,000 for government colleges (Rs 10,000 SC/BC/PwD), Rs 2,00,000 for private colleges. Fees already paid for a seat count towards it, and anyone who has already paid more than Rs 2,00,000 pays no more; for Round 3, fees paid equal to the security mean no new deposit if no penalty was imposed, otherwise the remaining (proportionate) amount must be paid. A Round 2 depositor who got no seat needn't deposit again for Round 3. In Round 3, joiners seeking an upgrade pay a security 'equivalent to the penalty amount'.
lose: Not joining a Round 2, Round 3 or stray seat; leaving a Round 2 seat, or a Round 1 seat after the free exit; an admission cancelled after allotment 'due to any reason' (for example wrong information at registration, or missing documents).
back: Refunds start only after all the rounds are over. The security deposit is refundable unless forfeited; if you join a seat, it is deducted from the balance of your six-month fee. A Round 1 free exit refunds the fees paid for the seat, not the application fee, if you take part in no later round.
leave: Service bond: Rs 30 lakh for 3 years; all-India quota Rs 20 lakh for 2 years (2025 corrigendum); in-service PCMS doctors Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh under the 2019 Health Department memo. Leaving midway: the balance fee for the whole course, if the college took a bond for it.
